audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the already-audited mirror: the page had Levels 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Sett, First item Skill and 2+ items Skill.
audit.why: The mirror set L1-L3 Sett, L4-5 Sett, L6 Skill, First item Sett, 2+ items Dr. Mundo — the packet chart with Level 6 moved to Skill for a mechanical reason: Maximum Dosage is 120s, the same as The Show Stopper, and it heals a percentage of his missing health, so slamming him low does not end the fight. whys[6] on this page already said two items flips to Mundo while win[6] rendered Skill.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4, 5 and 6 set to Sett / Skill / Sett / Dr. Mundo as one atomic paired group across both layers, with ratings and the four whys/phases lines rewritten to argue for the side now shown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper was tracked on every panel as 'his sustain spike + reset' with no cooldown, and the level-6 spike promised a kill that Maximum Dosage undoes.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and stores a portion of the damage he takes, healing him for a share of it on the burst — so feeding it damage is what powers it. Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s at 975 range on current health. Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: 17s written into the cooldown panel, the do's and report[5], with the store-and-heal mechanism stated; 120s and the missing-health heal written into spikes[1] and phases[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentioned Goes Where He Pleases. Sett's entire pattern is built on landing Facebreaker, and Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him outright.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction in the matchup and it appeared nowhere in either layer. A Sett who opens with Facebreaker gets no stun at all — the correct play is to make him spend the passive first, or to accept that the opener is a slow. Two further gaps: Blunt Force Trauma is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the cue rather than the cast; and Haymaker's true-damage centre is the one part of your kit his stacked resistances do nothing about.
audit.corrected: The passive stated in dontsFull[0].d, the cooldown panel, report[5], late and wants.foe[0]; the auto-reset tell written into spikes[2]; the true-damage-vs-resistances point into phases[3] and mid. Also corrected 'passive cheat-death' in late — the passive is an immobilise resist, not a death prevention.

edits.after: Stridebreaker sticks you to him, and Executioner's Calling on the same back is what makes the chip stick. Force trades while Bonesaw is spent.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Heart Zapper and commit on the gap.
edits.after: His health and regen scaling outrun your single-target damage. Haymaker's true centre still bites, but you win on the map now, not in the duel.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain spike + reset. All-in when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Dr. Mundo Infected Bonesaw: Throws a cleaver that slows and deals %current-HP magic damage; refunds HP. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1; it stores the damage you feed it and heals a share of that back on the burst. - Dr. Mundo Goes Where He Pleases: his passive resists the first immobilise, so your Facebreaker stun can simply be eaten.

edits.before: Through 3-6 you stay ahead: your E Facebreaker plus Q burst wins short trades, and your level 6 R slam chunks him before Maximum Dosage regen comes online, forcing him to ult defensively instead of fighting.
edits.after: Through 3-5 you stay ahead: Facebreaker plus Knuckle Down wins short trades, and Haymaker's true-damage centre ignores the resistances he stacks. At 6 it evens out -- Maximum Dosage answers your slam.

edits.before: Once Dr. Mundo finishes his HP and regen items the matchup flips hard — his W Heart Zapper, passive cheat-death, and R self-heal make him unkillable to your single-target kit, so end the game before he out-scales you.
edits.after: Once Dr. Mundo finishes his HP and regen items it flips hard — Heart Zapper, an R that heals off missing health, and a passive that eats your stun make him unkillable to your kit. End the game early.

edits.before: Farm through your poke and heal it back with passive plus items
edits.after: Eat your first stun on his passive and heal the trade back

notes: The decisive interaction in this lane was missing from both layers entirely: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect, so Sett's opening Facebreaker stun — the hinge of every trade the page describes — can simply be eaten. The page also called that passive a 'cheat-death', which it is not. Separately, the level-6 spike promised a kill on a champion whose 120s ultimate heals a percentage of his missing health; the mirror had already moved that row to Skill and I matched it.
